title: Correlation between features, one pair or every pair
summary: Correlates features and returns a flat table of pairs with n, r and a p value. With a subject column it also returns the within-subject estimate beside the marginal one. With covariates it returns partial correlation.

third_party.name: scipy
third_party.note: Supplies the correlation and its p value.

environment.provenance: No image. A virtual environment built from the pin beside it, 86 packages.

activation.note: Entered by putting its bin directory first on PATH. Where python itself lives is the machine's business.

inputs.name: table
inputs.description: Samples by features, sample identifier in the first column.

outputs.name: pairs
outputs.description: One row per pair: x, y, n, r, p_value, and the within-subject columns when a subject column was given.

outputs.name: notes
outputs.description: What the primitive recorded about the estimate, including when it is partial and which cases were dropped.
outputs.interpretation: Not decoration. A result read without these is misread.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Columns to correlate. With y omitted, every unordered pair within x is returned.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Optional second set, giving a grid of x against y rather than pairs within x.

parameters.name: subject_col
parameters.description: Adds the repeated-measures estimate beside the marginal one.

parameters.name: covar_cols
parameters.description: Partial correlation, controlling for these columns. Complete cases are taken per pair.

resources.memory_hint: The whole grid is computed in one pass, so memory follows the table rather than the number of pairs.

interpretation: Nothing here is corrected for multiple testing. A grid is many tests, so a p value from it must be adjusted before anything is read as significant. When a subject column is given, the gap between the marginal and the within-subject estimate is the finding: a large marginal r with a small within-subject r means the association is between subjects rather than something tracking within a person over time.
notes: First entry in this domain. The adapter is shared by every statistics capability.
for_people: Correlates features against each other, one pair or every pair.
